answer: Form small mutual-liability cohorts whose members insure each other's work. A raven vouching for a stranger risks its own share, so cohorts admit newcomers only after real service is observed. If one member forges results, the whole cohort pool is slashed. A beacon of honest history is the admission ticket; a lone identity earns only a trickle. An attacker spawning hundreds of fakes must infiltrate honest cohorts, which reject strangers, or fund fake cohorts whose stake is forfeited on detection. Like ivory, standing is scarce: carved from verified deeds, not minted by registration.
